utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, kindly call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Today is Tuesday [as interpreted], 4th of March, 2009. Good morning, Mr. Pusic. Good morning, Mr. Praljak and Mr. Coric, good morning to Defence counsel, and all the representatives of the OTP under the helm of Mr. Stringer, and good morning to all the people assisting us. You have two IC numbers, don't you, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour. Some parties have submitted lists of documents to be tendered through Witness 2D-AB. The list submitted by 2D shall be given Exhibit IC 937, and the list submitted by the Prosecution shall be given Exhibit IC 938.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We're going to have a new witness. You will have two hours for Mr. Stojic. The Prosecutor will have two hours, and the other Defence counsel will have one hour. Without further adieu, let's have the witness brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir. Please state your surname, first name, and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dragan Pinjuh; 1963.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What date, precisely?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 13th of December, 1963.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your current occupation, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the moment, I'm retired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the army, from what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What was your rank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Major.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Sir, have you had an opportunity to testify before a court of law or is this going to be the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please read out the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. Please sit down. I think that Ms. Nozica explained to you how this is going to take place. She's going to ask questions of you and submit some 20 documents. Thereafter, the other accused [as interpreted] representing the other accused, if they think it's useful, will ask questions themselves, and then you have the OTP representatives on your right-hand side who are going to have the same time for their cross-examination as Ms. Nozica had for her examination-in-chief. And the four Judges in front of you may also ask questions of you, based on the documents we are given. So this is what I wanted to tell you. You now are a witness of the Court. In other words, you probably will continue your testimony tomorrow, but you're not supposed to have any contact whatsoever with anybody. If you fail to understand a question, do not hesitate to ask for clarification or for the question to be rephrased. If you're not feeling well, tell us so, and I'll have the doctor come straight away to have you examined. Otherwise, we can have a short break. But that's just in theory. So this should enable your testimony to unfold as smoothly as possible. You may proceed, Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, and everybody else in the courtroom. Your Honours, calculating the time left of the Stojic Defence, I shall endeavour to be as quick with this witness as possible so that we can divide the time up among the other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Pinjuh.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, I'd just shortly like to go through your CV and the posts you occupied, so I'll take it in order, and you'll just tell me whether what I'm saying is correct. You went to the Vocational Machine and Technical School in Sarajevo and completed that in 1982, and in 1994 you also graduated from the additional police training course. On the 18th of September, 1991, you were engaged as a reservist of the MUP of BH in Sarajevo. On the 6th of April, 1992, you became the commander of the Pofalici Company within the frameworks of the TO in Novo Sarajevo in Sarajevo. At the beginning of June, 1992, when the HVO was established in Sarajevo, you became the commander of the battalion of the HVO in Novo Sarajevo. On the 29th of December, 1992, you were appointed the deputy president of the brigade of the HVO -- correction. I meant to say "deputy commander" of the brigade of the HVO, called Kralj Tvrtko in Sarajevo. From the end of April 1993, you found yourself in Medjugorje, and up until that time you otherwise lived in Sarajevo. On the 15th of August, 1993, you were relieved of your duties as deputy commander of the HVO, the Kralj Tvrtko Brigade, and until December 1993, you were placed at the disposal of the office for the defence of Grude. From December 1993 onwards, you relocated to Mostar to take up your duties there as commander of the unit for the protection and security of facilities and individuals of special importance of the MUP of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. In 19 -- yes, that's right. In 1997, you became employed in a private firm, a security firm, and in 1999 you got a job in the National Security Service of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And after that, in 2005, you retired. Are all -- is that information correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, at the beginning of June, as we said reading out your CV, when the HVO of Sarajevo was established, did you -- were you appointed to a post?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. I was appointed commander of the Novo Sarajevo Battalion, and I was appointed by the then president of the HVO, Velimir Maric.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In addition to the battalion in Sarajevo, at that time were there other -- any other HVO battalions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. There was one in Sarajevo, which was the 1st Battalion with its seat at Stup, Ilidza municipality. There was the 2nd Battalion in the Novi Grad municipality, and the 4th Battalion in Centar, the municipality of Stari Grad.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, was a brigade, an HVO brigade, established in Sarajevo, and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, a brigade was formed in December 1992, and its name was Kralj Tvrtko.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know who appointed -- who was appointed commander of the brigade and who that was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: The brigade commander became Mr. Slavko Zelic, and he was appointed by the president, Mate Boban.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know when the other officers were appointed and in what way, how they came to be in the Command of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: At the proposal of the command of the brigade, Slavko Zelic, the Command of the brigade was appointed, and the head of the Defence Department, Mr. Bruno Stojic, made those appointments.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, to the best of your recollections, when that occurred?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: That was at the end of December 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In addition to this military section of the HVO in Sarajevo, was there a civilian section of the HVO, and if so, as of what date?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, it did. There was the Municipal Council of the HVO as a civilian body, as a civilian council, and with the Defence Department in Sarajevo, it came to be established, and the first president was Velimir Maric. And later on, Mr. Slavko Zelic was appointed president of the Croatian Defence Council in Sarajevo, and as far as I remember he was appointed in March 1993 by the president of the HVO, Mr. Jadranko Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We are talking about 1992 here; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you to look at the binder. If you haven't been provided with it, you will be. And I'd like us to look at some of the documents we've -- referring to the events and appointments we've just been discussing. Witness, would you look at document 2D 1185 now, please, and that should be the first document in your binder. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So this is a letter to be handed to Mr. Slavko Zelic in person, and it is from the head of the Defence Department, Bruno Stojic. The date is the 5th of December, 1992. And from this letter, we can see that Mr. Zelic had already been appointed commander of the brigade by Mr. Boban, as you said, and he is being asked to send in a list of the Command, the persons to take up their positions in the Command, with all their CV and data, so that these individuals could be appointed. And it says that the brigade will be named the Kralj Tvrtko Brigade. Now, do you know that Mr. Slavko Zelic did indeed do this and send in a proposal for the men to make up the Command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, and Slavko compiled this proposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And now take a look at the next document, which is 2D 1177. And tell me when you've found it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a letter of appointment by Mr. Bruno Stojic, dated the 29th of December, of the Command of the Kralj Tvrtko Brigade in Sarajevo; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And you are under number 1 as the deputy commander. Now I'd like you to turn to the second page, where we can see that the document was sent to the Brigade Command, the Main Staff, and what is particularly important, to the Personnel Department. Now, Mr. Pinjuh, do you know that the Brigade Command was kept a record of, and in the Personnel Department of the Defence Department in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'd like you now to look at the next document, which is P 1778, P 1778, as I said, and this is the 33rd session of the Croatian Defence Council, as we can see from this document. And I'd like to ask you to turn to page 5 in both the English and Croatian versions. And I'd like to emphasise that the date of this session is the 1st of April, 1993. And on page 5, under item 8, we see that in the HVO of the Sarajevo municipality, Slavko Zelic is being appointed as president?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And then on the second page, we have the entire Presidency, and the HVO commissioners in the various municipalities, Stari Grad, Novo Sarajevo, Novi Grad, and Ilidza; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So that is, in fact, the decision taken by the HVO HZ-HB on the appointment of the Presidency, when Mr. Zelic was appointed president; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you now, Mr. Pinjuh, to explain to the Trial Chamber how the battalions and HVO brigades or, rather, the Kralj Tvrtko Brigade was distributed in Sarajevo. What lines did they hold?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: The HVO units in Sarajevo included four battalions. The 1st Battalion held its line in the area of responsibility of the Stup settlement. The 2nd and 3rd Battalion held the line along the Miljacka River, the Novo Sarajevo municipality towards Malin Vor, and the 4th was the Protection Battalion providing security for various facilities and had the role of intervention as an intervention battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This deployment and disposition of the battalions of the HVO Kralj Tvrtko Brigade or, rather, battalion, was that in agreement with the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, that was done in cooperation and in agreement with the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And for how long did this line along the Miljacka River, as you said -- how long did it exist?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Until the 6th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, could you explain to the Trial Chamber now how important this line was, especially that line along the Miljacka River that you mentioned which, as we can see, was held by your battalion? What was its importance, in terms of defence? How important was it, in terms of the defence of the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: That line was right in the center of the city of Sarajevo between the Novo Sarajevo and Centar municipalities, and if the line fell, then Sarajevo would be split into two parts, and most probably life would be very different and the military positions would be very different, and the city might even have fallen.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The line was on the Miljacka River?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, can you please tell me what was the ethnic composition of the Kralj Tvrtko HVO Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, before Ms. Nozica addresses this issue, I'm now discovering things with you. I didn't know at all that until November 1993 the HVO was in Sarajevo in agreement with the ABiH, so this is something that comes into play and that I wasn't at all aware of, which might change quite a few things indeed. I must ask you follow-up questions. If I understand properly, it was during this siege of Sarajevo by the Serbs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the common enemy, HVO -- I asked you something, but we didn't get your answer on record. I'll ask you again. Sir, it was during the siege of Sarajevo by the Serbs? So please answer that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that was during the Serb siege.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In other words, until November 1993, the HVO and the ABiH had a common enemy, the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In purely military terms, because you had somehow the space in Sarajevo spread between you, and you said just as well you were there because otherwise Sarajevo would have fallen quickly. As the four HVO battalions and ABiH were spread, who was your counterpart on the ABiH side? Who was your counterpart?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mustafa Hajrulahovic, Talijan, was the commander of the 1st Corps, and his deputy was Vehid Karavelic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it was Mustafa, whose surname was not put on record, who was your counterpart. Does this mean that on a daily basis, there were telephone or physical contacts between the HVO and the ABiH in order to face the Serb enemy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we did cooperate in a number of sectors, military, logistics, and as needed in some other sectors as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: And was this some permanent cooperation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was constant when we were holding the line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When did it cease?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 6th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for all your answers.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would just like to ask to make a correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said Mustafa Hajrulahovic, Talijan, was the commander of the 1st Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And Mr. Kraljevic was his deputy; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, he was his deputy and later commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And when he was deputy, that was his rank, and you cooperated with him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I asked you about that earlier, but now that His Honour, the Judge, put that question, you had joint meetings and coordinated in all important things?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. Commander Zelic mostly did that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Were you present at those meetings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Occasionally when I was in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And this disposition, this deployment of the units that were holding the line around Sarajevo was absolutely in agreement with the 1st Corps of the Bosnia-Herzegovinian Army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you like that, and you can tell Their Honours because they don't know that perhaps. Do you agree that one of the lines that the HVO was holding was one of the most important lines at the time when the HVO was there, in view of the geographical layout, because in that section the line of separation was a river? I cannot hear you. What you're nodding is not good enough. We would need to have that on the transcript. But now my colleague is on her feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning to Your Honours, and everyone in and around the courtroom, Witness. I would have to object to the line of questioning by Ms. Nozica here, and I get up to object to leading question. And, in particular, on page 12, line 9, the question is asked: "Do you agree that one of the lines ..." And I would ask for counsel to phrase her questions more openly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. Thank you, thank you, thank you, I will rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: How important for the defence of the town of Sarajevo -- I already asked you that, but I'm asking you because of the geographical nature of that line. What was it, in terms of its layout, the line that the HVO was holding?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: The line was very important for the defence of the town of Sarajevo, because in the center of town itself, in the Novo Sarajevo municipality, the Serbian Army had entered Grbavica, which was the urban part of the town, and that is where the Miljacka River flows. On the other side, there were the Marshal Tito Barracks, where the JNA Army was still situated. And then two kilometres further along was the border with the Serbian army towards Vogosca, so if the line fell the area of Grbavica would join up with the lines in Valesici and Gornji Pofalici, and that is why -- and the barracks, Marshal Tito, and that is why the town would be cut in two parts, because the line -- that was why the line was important. And otherwise the town would have been cut in two parts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, there were International Observers there. Were they aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We had our own officer, liaison officer, who was with the UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, your liaison officer would explain to the UNPROFOR everything about the cooperation? Everybody was aware?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We are now going to move to the numbers. We are now talking about figures that are known to you. Can you tell me the strength of the HVO Kralj Tvrtko Brigade and what was the ethnic composition of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: The Kralj Tvrtko Brigade was some 1800 men strong. The ethnic composition was 50 per cent members of the Croatian ethnicity, and the rest were Bosniaks and Serbs, as well as representatives of the ethnic minorities, such as the Hungarian, Czech, Roma, Jewish, and others.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you please tell me the weapons that your brigade had?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Our brigade was an infantry brigade, and it had infantry weaponry, for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And how was this weaponry obtained?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: With organising the defence and the formation of units in Sarajevo, the first weapons were personal weapons or weapons issued through the MUP or the TO. Later, with the liberation of the barracks in Sarajevo, some weapons were seized and were distributed to the HVO and the B and H Army units.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And can you please tell me, in 1992, did you receive any weapons from the HVO Mostar Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: From what I know, the logistics support and weapons and ammunition did come from that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you briefly tell me how it came into the town, physically? And I don't want to put leading questions, but was the town at that time already under siege by the Serbian Army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Which period are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The end of 1991 and later, end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: It usually came by military routes via Igman.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you explain to Their Honours what that means, via military paths? Did somebody carry it, transfer it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Mostly, it was physically carried by -- on foot.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you please tell me if this provision of supplies and weapons from Mostar -- was the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina informed about that, and did you do this in cooperation with them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, they were informed about it, and they didn't pose any problems for this kind of thing to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said that the HVO in Sarajevo also had a liaison officer with the UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you please tell me who that was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: That was Mr. Anton Rill.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Anton Rill. Can you tell Their Honours, based on your experience, if you know - I'm interested in only what you know - what was the task of that officer, liaison officer? What did he do that you knew of?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, it was our intention, through the liaison officer with the UNPROFOR, to inform the UNPROFOR about all that was happening in the HVO and in the town of Sarajevo, and also to see how the citizens of the town of Sarajevo could be helped, also the HVO, from UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, did you remain in Sarajevo that whole time? Now we see that in December, you were appointed deputy commander of the Kralj Tvrtko HVO Brigade. Were you in Sarajevo the whole time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: No. In late 1992, pursuant to a decision of the brigade HQ, was sent to the Mostar area, to the Defence Department, in order to secure logistical support for our brigade in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you go out of Sarajevo, and with whom did you leave?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: I left in January under military police escort.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We're talking about 1993 now, are we?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And what you say, military police escort, was that somebody from your brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, it was the brigade military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you -- did you -- let me ask you this: In this period up to January 1993, did you have any communications with Sarajevo -- with Mostar? Excuse me. Were you able to communicate with Mostar from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: We didn't have any direct connections, only communication through Hamm radio operators. We could speak with somebody from Herzegovina or sometimes through the high representative who worked in the high-ranking bodies of the authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you came to Mostar, who received you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: When I came to Mostar, we went to see the chief of the Defence Department and his deputy, Mr. Bozic, and that day we also met Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And what was the topic of these meetings that day in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: We informed the gentlemen about the situation and all that was going on in Sarajevo, and we asked for specific assistance in materiel and equipment.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And did you receive any support or promises from Mr. Stojic and from Mr. Praljak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, we did receive support, and everything that they told us then was later implemented.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you explain to them which positions the HVO was holding in town?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, we told them what our positions were.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And did you receive support, in terms of that, to continue with these activities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, we received full support for our participation in the defence of the town of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: After this meeting, did you take any steps in order to obtain the materiel and equipment required for the defence of Sarajevo by your brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: After the meeting, we organised a convoy to transfer weapons to Sarajevo. We went to the Logistics Centre in Grude and told them what we needed, and requested the necessary passes from the 4th Corps. Then we brought the weapons in.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Where did you bring them in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: We brought the weapons to the relocated Logistics Centre in Kiseljak. That was the one for the HVO of Sarajevo. And then we organised the transfer of that to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you say the Logistics Centre in Kiseljak, was this a logistics centre of your brigade, the Kralj Tvrtko Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you please explain to the Chamber why it was necessary for you to have a logistics centre in Kiseljak? What were the reasons for that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I would like to get back to the visit you made in January, where you met Mr. Stojic, Bozic, and General Praljak. According to what we understood, you asked them for their support, for logistical and arms support. When you addressed them, did you address them as Croats from Herzegovina or were you addressing the Republic of Croatia? When you were asking for help, who did you turn to, exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The HZ-HB HVO Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A subsidiary question: Did they tell you that they could provide you with equipment, or did they say that you needed to wait? What did they say, exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They said that they were supporting us and that we should go to the Central Logistics Centre in Grude, headed by Mr. Ante Jelavic, and to see what we can get, what they had available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that's what you did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And my last question was what this Logistics Centre in Kiseljak was, and why was it in Kiseljak, and you said it was a logistics centre of your brigade. I asked you why it had to be located in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: We made a decision to set up a logistics centre in Kiseljak because it was the closest to Sarajevo. It was like a logistics warehouse, where we would assemble the weapons and the required materiel and equipment and distribute it to Sarajevo from there, when possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Witness, to make things absolutely clear, in Sarajevo -- you couldn't enter Sarajevo by car at that time, could you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, after leaving Sarajevo, did you leave anymore times for -- to procure materiel and equipment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. In March, we needed anti-armoured devices because tanks were used against us, so we needed some anti-armour devices, and we organised another trip to the Logistical Centre to try and procure those vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Witness, before we move on to this other trip of yours, are we talking about the 1st January and December and -- January and February of 1993, was that when Sarajevo had a lack of materiel and technical equipment and food, and was that indeed the most difficult time in Sarajevo after the aggression of the Serb Army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, that year was a terrible year.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'll again have to object to leading questions. I'm asking for counsel to phrase her questions more openly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, please avoid leading questions. What I'm interested in are the answers, not so much the way questions are put. As a judge, I know how to weigh the questions, whether they are a leading question or not. The Prosecution feels this is a question of principle, so please rephrase your questions so that we don't have objections.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I understand that completely, and we did raise the same objections during the Prosecution case, so I'll do my best not to ask leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Anyway, what was the end of 1992 like and the beginning of 1993 in Sarajevo, from the aspects of weapons, the weaponry that the army had, the military activities, the humanitarian situation, electricity, water, and all the rest of it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: During that period, Sarajevo faced a very difficult situation. It was a very cold winter. There was no heating, no electricity, no water either. It was very cold. All the stocks that we had had been exhausted, food stocks and everything else, and it was a truly difficult situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Was that one of the reasons for which you were given this assignment to try and procure material and resources from the HVO Mostar for the Kralj Tvrtko Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. We had enough manpower, but we needed logistics, logistical support, mostly. We had enough long barrels, but not food and all the rest of it. We kept having a shortage of food, medicines, and many other things.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you explain briefly what your second trip was like and what happened along the way, en route?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, I decided to set out on that journey again. We set out, and we came across a check-point before entering Konjic municipality, a check-point that wasn't there before, and we were stopped there by members of the BH Army. And after inspecting our documents, they allowed us to pass through. And at Jablanica, we came across another check-point. We showed our IDs again, talked to the men there, asked that they let us through, and they did. So I realised that there were check-points set up along that free part of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And that was the first time that you saw these check-points?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. The first time I went, there were no check-points, and I had no problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You had permission from the 1st Corps of the BH Army and all the necessary papers and documents showing that you were going from Sarajevo and that you were a member of the Sarajevo HVO; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you reach Mostar?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And did you undertake any measures to organise a convoy?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: We went to Grude. We were put up in Citluk. We went to Grude, the Logistical Centre there, and tried to see how many anti-armoured vehicles we could procure and to see how we were going to transport them, bring them in.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: As we did our best to procure the material we needed and to see how we were going to get them to where they were needed, through the media and in talking to people, we see -- saw that something was happening in that general area, that there were conflicts and clashes between the HVO and BH Army, skirmishes, especially in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And what period was that? You said you set out in March, but what period are you referring to now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: It was the end of March and beginning of April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you hear anything specific about what happened in Konjic at the end of March?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: At the time, I was in Citluk and I heard there that the BH Army had attacked HVO units in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, thank you. And regardless of that, you decided to return to Sarajevo, did you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: No, we decided that we couldn't, given the present circumstances, take the same route back, so we returned the weapons -- or, rather, we left them in Grude.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But did you set out towards Sarajevo, nonetheless?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: We waited for a time to see what the developments were going to be, and after some time had passed we decided to go back to Sarajevo, because that's where we came from.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, tell us who set out on the journey?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, we received some humanitarian assistance first in Siroki Brijeg to take to the defenders' families, some food and things like that, and then we loaded them up into a truck and set out for Sarajevo on the 15th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I see. The 15th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: I think that was the date, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And what happened along your route?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, the logistics people and the military policemen, with a small truck, went in front of me. I followed them. And before entering Jablanica, the road was closed at a check-point, and I was stopped by the BH Army. And when I got out to explain to them that I had all my papers in order, a member of the BH Army hit me with his rifle-butt. He hit me in my face. And they then took me to the Jablanica police station, and they took my side-arms and vehicle, and seized my documents and told me to wait, that I was to speak to their security officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did he come? Did you have that conversation, that interview?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Several hours later, he did appear, and we did have that conversation. Well, interview.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What happened afterwards? Were your papers and vehicle returned to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: No, my side-arms and vehicle were not returned. The papers had to be checked out, and I had to stay there for several days while they inspected my papers.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: I was on the premises of that police station all the time, waiting, waiting every day for my documents to be returned so that I could continue my journey towards Sarajevo. I thought that I would ultimately be able to reach Sarajevo, but after some time had gone by I realised that I wasn't going to be allowed to pass, that the conflicts had already begun, and I decided to take another route and go back to Herzegovina across the mountains.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And did you do that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Fine. Now, after that, you said that that was -- that you set out for Mostar on the 15th of April; right? So that was sometime around the beginning of May. Have I calculated that properly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, the end of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I see, the end of April 1993. Where did you go to Herzegovina, specifically?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: I went to Medjugorje.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I see, Medjugorje. Tell me, please, after that, did you ever go back to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And you live in Herzegovina to this day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: I live in the Mostar area, but I have a house in Sarajevo, where my father lives, so I very often go to Sarajevo and travel between Mostar and Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Now, with respect to logistical support, I'd like to ask you to look at some documents. 2D 1195 is the first one. I think that's the next document in order in your binder. 2D 1195 is the number. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, this is a letter from the commander of the Kralj Tvrtko Brigade, Slavko Zelic, on the 25th of February, 1993. He is sent to the Main Staff in Mostar -- it's been sent to the Main Staff in Mostar. And from the first part of that letter, we see that he says that the HVO of Sarajevo has for some time been trying to procure materiel and technical equipment for the Kralj Tvrtko Brigade, and he says that the results are minimal because they weren't able to organise a sufficiently secure channel for bringing in those resources. So was that the reason for your trip, as you said earlier on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In the second part of this letter, we see that there was very good cooperation with the Ministry of the Interior of Sarajevo, and suggestions are made that certain persons from this ministry, together with the HVO, could procure some weapons. Did you know Mr. Drina Faruk, Nedzad Cengic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: As for Mr. Drina Faruk, I have heard of him, his name is familiar, but I haven't heard of Nedzad Cengic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Now, at the end of this letter, it says: "Our needs are based on 1.000 completely unequipped soldiers with regards to the position which we are currently holding in our area of responsibility at Stup and Dobrinja, we feel the greatest shortages in anti-armour resources. With current equipment, the brigade which consists of 1650 men, divided into four battalions, possesses 250 barrels and very scarce quantity of ammunition." And then the 60-millimetre mortars are mentioned, and two hand-held rocket-launchers for which they need ammunition. Now, Mr. Pinjuh, do you know that those were the requirements and the needs, and is that what you've been telling us about so far, that those were the reasons for your trips?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, that was what we needed in order to hold the line.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And from this letter, we can clearly see the HVO Kralj Tvrtko Brigade, cooperation with the Main Staff of the Defence Department in Mostar; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you to look at the next document, which is 2D 1178. Would you explain what this is to Their Honours?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. Well, because of the logistical needs for materiel and technical equipment, we used this occasion to procure food and clothing for the families of the defenders of Sarajevo, so this is a shipping record which we received from Caritas at Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, Witness, the food mentioned here, was it transported in a truck that you said went out together with you on the 15th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. Later on, I learnt that they managed to reach Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's just go back a bit. So that's when you were held back at Jablanica, right, and the truck managed to get through to Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know how they managed to do that, but I assume they had the papers necessary from the humanitarian organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Witness, after April 1993, as you yourself said, you were not -- no longer able to return to Sarajevo. Did you have any contact whatsoever with members of the Kralj Tvrtko Brigade in Sarajevo, and if so, what were your contacts in the coming period? And we'll limit ourselves until the 6th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, the only contacts that I could have with the HVO of Sarajevo during that period of -- were via the radio Hamms in Grude and Ljubuski. I would make an appointment for having a conversation with our liaison officer, and I would come in at that time, and with the radio Hamms, I would be connected and I would ask whether there were any wounded and things like that. Now, in August I mentioned Mr. -- I met Mr. Slavko Zelic in Grude, so I talked to him personally about what the situation was like in Sarajevo, what was happening, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Just to refresh our memories, could you tell the Trial Chamber again what Slavko Zelic was at the time after April 1993, at the time when you met him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: He was president of the Croatian Defence Council in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So that's the civilian part, the civilian section; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And what did he tell you? What did he say the situation was like in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: He said that it was -- it had become impossible to have the HVO in Sarajevo and that the BH Command demanded that the HVO be disbanded, that the HVO soldiers should become part and parcel of the BH Army, that they should be one and the same army.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So when you saw him, and that was at the end of August, you say, 1993, did he tell you which lines were still controlled by the HVO in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: As far as I understood him, it held the same lines, but he did tell me that the line along the Miljacka River had been expanded by one kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, what happened on the 6th of November, 1993, in Sarajevo with your -- to your brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: On the 6th of November, the BH Army launched an attack on all positions, and the headquarters of the HVO of Sarajevo and the brigade, and disarmed the HVO and the brigade, and they arrested all their members.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know who was arrested, specifically?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: The president of the HVO, Slavko Zelic, was arrested; the brigade commander, Ivan Vulic; along with a few other people that I can't tell you the names of now. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: As you were in Mostar yourself, or, rather, Medjugorje at that time, tell me how you came to learn about this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: First of all, the information came to me through the media, on the news bulletins, and later on people talked about it -- or, rather, it appeared in the press, and we heard what happened in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Just to correct line 9 of page 28, you said Vulic, I believe, was the name you mentioned, Slavko Vulic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: No, Ivan Vulic was the name, and Slavko Zelic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I see, thank you. So you heard about this on television, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And do you know what happened after that with the Kralj Tvrtko Brigade in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: The brigade was transformed into the B and H -- into a B and H Army brigade, which was called the Hrvatska Brigada, and the commander who was appointed to the brigade was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So was the HVO Brigade in Sarajevo abolished, practically?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, very well. Now I'm going to ask you to look at some documents about that. Can we please look at document 2D 01 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm trying to understand how the brigade you belonged to was transformed. It turned into the Croatian Brigade of the ABiH. From what we understand, there was an attack on the positions of the HVO on the 6th of December, and people are captured and disarmed. Everybody was disarmed. When the Croatian Brigade was formed, were there weapons handed over to the Croats again, were they told that they were a Croatian brigade as part of the ABiH? Is that how things happened or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 6th of December, in the morning, a special unit of the B and H Army and the police attacked the positions and the headquarters of the HVO. After that, members of the HVO were arrested and taken to certain rooms, such as the Alija Alagic School in Novo Sarajevo, which is where they kept them detained. And as I later found out, a lot of people were beaten, abused. They were forced to swallow the Croatian markings that they wore. The Croatian flag was taken down and thrown away. Then those people were individually placed in the new brigade which was part of the B and H Army, and it was named the Hrvatska Brigade, probably for some political reasons that I'm not aware of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And when the ABiH took control of the brigade, were there casualties, dead or injured people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were no dead. I know that there were some wounded, yes, and some people were beaten. When the disarming took place, the HVO did not put up any resistance, any military resistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. But this line that was occupied by the Croats, was it held by the same people or were Muslim ABiH soldiers put there to replace the HVO unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From what I heard, other units were brought there to guard that line, and then later this new brigade was supposed to again take up some of those lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please continue, Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Witness, let us first make a correction. On page 29, line 16, you said that this intervention against the brigade was carried out by the Bosnia and Herzegovina Army and the MUP. We don't have that in the transcript, that the Bosnia and Herzegovina Army and the MUP made this intervention in relation to the HVO brigade.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, special units of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you please explain this? The newly-formed Croatian Brigade, did it have a completely different status and composition than the HVO Kralj Tvrtko Brigade? Can you please explain the status and composition issue?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: It had a completely different position within the B and H Army. It was exactly the same as any other unit or formation within the B and A Army. I think it had some sort of a number, 141st or something Infantry Brigade. We were part before of the units in the Bosnia and Herzegovina Army, but this new brigade was a part of the B and H Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And was the HVO unit practically part of the armed forces in the defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, we were always considered to be a part of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, the newly-formed brigade was a brigade of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we now look at a few documents about these events. These are documents 2D 1193 -- can you please tell me when you find the document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a letter from Mr. Boban. Through Mr. Pogarcic, his adviser, that he's sending to General Francis Briquemont, the commander of UNPROFOR. The document is dated the 2nd of October, 1993, so this is before all of these events?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In this first part of the letter, Mr. Boban writes about the ultimatum that evidently the 1st Corps issued to the HVO at that time, and it talks about how important the Kralj Tvrtko Brigade was in the defence of Sarajevo, how many of its members were killed. It talks about a large percentage, in terms of the overall percentage of the Croatian population, which is 8 per cent, and how many Croats were killed in the conflict, and he's asking for these activities to be stopped, the ones that were leading to the abolishment of the Kralj Tvrtko Brigade, and the consequences of what -- of that, if that were to happen. And it says this is one of the most openly-addressed public calls to ethnic cleansing and genocide against the Croats. Later, did this actually take place? The ultimatum was not withdrawn, and after that did it actually happen that the brigade was abandoned, abolished, and that never existed again?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, the brigade was abolished, and you can see on the basis of this letter that the heads of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna were informed about the steps that the B and H Army would take in relation to the Sarajevo HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you look at 2D 01188? That's the next document. The Presidency of the HDZ City Board is sending a letter on the 9th of November, 1993, to the president of the B and H Republic and the prime minister of the republic, but you can see from this first part that it was a kind of public proclamation, where also all the events of the 16th of November, 1993, are explained. But there is something very interesting that is said here about the attitude of the armija before these events, and this is somewhere in the second paragraph, third sentence, where it says: "For the contribution of the Croats in the defence of the city, as well as exceptionally good cooperation, 15 days ago the commanders of the HVO units were commended publicly by Dr. Karavelic, the commander of the 1st Corps ..." This is the gentleman that you mentioned who for a while was the deputy commander and then the commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Does this not indicate, in fact, Mr. Pinjuh, without us going into any kind of speculation about why the Bosnia-Herzegovina Army did that in that particular period --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may, I apologise for my interruption again, but once again there is a leading question from counsel on page 33, line 2: "Does this not indicate, in fact ..." And I again ask for more openly-phrased questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] THE COURT: You are right. Please rephrase your question, Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, does this document indicate that cooperation up until 15 days before the events with the Bosnia and Herzegovina Army was professional?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: I am convinced that it was professional from our side.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to ask you to look at the next document. This is 1D 2173. And please tell me when you've found the document.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. This is another document. I would like to ask the Prosecutor to turn her microphone off, if possible. We are being disturbed, and we can also hear everything, and that is not quite good. Anyway, this is another document from the 9th of November, 1993, signed by Stjepan Pocernja [phoen]. It's sent to the president of the republic, Franjo Tudjman, Mate Boban, Jadranko Prlic, Mr. Slobodan Praljak. They are all being informed about what happened with the HVO Kralj Tvrtko Brigade in Sarajevo. Does this also confirm what you told us? You knew about what happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, it was publicly known with what had happened in Sarajevo, and everybody began to react, whoever was concerned about it, and they asked for protection of the Croatian people in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, did a large number of Croats move out of Sarajevo after these events?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: I think that this did have an effect on the relationship between Croats and Bosniaks in Sarajevo and that Croats, for this reason, decided to leave Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you to look at document 2D 01179. Witness, can you please tell us what this is about? What is this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: This is a document issued in 1997 about all those who were -- Croats who were killed defending Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We have three HVO, HOS, and the Kralj Tvrtko Croatian Brigade insignia. I'm only going to ask you about HOS. At the time when you were a member of the brigade, the Kralj Tvrtko Brigade, did you cooperate in Sarajevo with the HOS?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: We knew that it existed, but we did not think it was necessary for them to -- well, we thought a it would be good for them to join the HVO brigades, but actually they continued to operate under the direct command of the Bosnia and Herzegovina Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand properly, because all this is very complex, the HOS was under the direct command of the ABiH, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was part of their forces under this name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who was the commander of the HOS in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Matanovic, something like that. I'm not quite sure, but it's something that is easy to find out. Matosin, something like that. I knew who it was at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this HOS unit, I guess that there were also Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, mostly Croats and Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So they were mostly Croats and Bosniaks. Do you know the ratio?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that there were more Bosniaks than Croats, because the Croats mostly took up the high-ranking or leadership positions within the HOS, and that the Bosniaks, who accepted the HOS programme, constituted its forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where were the HOS units deployed in and around Sarajevo that were part of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that they had lines that they were holding. I think that they were billeted in a school that was used as a temporary war facility, and they were billeted there, they were staying there. I don't know what sort of tasks they were carrying out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, we have a list, as part of this document, that lists the members of these three units. This is a list of what?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: These are the defenders of the HVO who were killed, and then the HOS defenders, and the defenders of the Kralj Tvrtko Brigade. All of them were defending Sarajevo and were killed. The Kralj Tvrtko Brigade was later disbanded.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When we're talking about the members of the Kralj Tvrtko HVO Brigade who were killed, the data refers mostly to 1992, and they indicate the number of those killed from the Croatian Kralj Tvrtko Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, we have 100 names here in this list. Are these definitive numbers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: I think this is a document from 1997. Today, I think we have a complete record and that there were many more ethnic Croats who were killed in the defence of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now I'm going to move to a topic that deals with the convoy of citizens who left Sarajevo, so now I'm just briefly going to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I believe Ms. Nozica made a mistake. I'm looking at the list of these hundred individuals who were killed. I can see that some were killed in 1992, others in 1993, and also in 1994.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are three coats of arms, one for those killed in 1992 and 1993 as members of the HVO, those who were killed in 1994 were members of this new brigade that was part of the Bosnia and Herzegovina Army, and there were some members of the HOS as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as you know, were most of these people killed in 1992, in 1993, or in 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Most of them were killed in 1992 and 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I asked you to look at 2D 00454. Witness, I would just like you to tell me when you find the document.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: I have found the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a document of the 7th of April, 1994. It's already become an exhibit, so it's not necessary to go through it. I'm only interested in one thing. You mentioned the liaison officer of the HVO in Sarajevo, Mr. Rill, Anton, and at the top there is his name?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, April 7th, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When the convoy of citizens was leaving Sarajevo, did you, the HVO Brigade in Sarajevo, have any assignments? Did you help in any way when this was going on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Any time a convoy was organised, our military police from the brigade was charged with taking the citizens to the convoy from wherever they were departing from in Sarajevo, and we were always available to all the humanitarian organisations, if they needed any assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, Mr. Rill, did he have the task of ensuring free passage for the convoy further on, upon leaving Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, if he was included in the convoys, then that would have been one of his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I would like to avoid to do the same again and again, but I would also like you -- to ask you, Ms. Nozica, and also the witness, really to slow down, to speak only after a break after a question, and then answer, because it is -- it cannot be followed. And it was by this Bench many times stressed that it is in your interest that everything should be recorded completely, which is in your interests for us to read and to know. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, I am doing my best, and looking at the transcript as well, and I see that the questions and answers are being recorded. But I assume it's a little more difficult to interpret.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, I asked you yesterday to make pauses, Witness, between my questions and your answers, but we get carried away, I suppose. I was asking you about what you knew about the role of Mr. Rill or, rather, the liaison officer, upon the convoy leaving Sarajevo. Do you know what his duties were in that regard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: His duties were to inform UNPROFOR about the convoy and to try and get permission for its free passage through areas held by the HVO for destinations in third countries or in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's look at 2D 1190 now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. You've just said something in passing very quickly. It may have escaped everybody, but for me, because I'm listening to your every word. If I understand properly, there were convoys leaving Sarajevo. People would get into buses, because we can see there are numbers of buses, and these people would leave Sarajevo. And then you added something, but very quickly, so quickly that it was difficult to follow. You said that these people might go to Croatia or to third countries. Does this mean that there was or there were people, Croats, Serbs, or Muslims, I don't know, going from Sarajevo to Croatia or to third countries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, those convoys were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So these convoys were organised. And did these people leave in order to go somewhere safe or did they go for other reasons? You see, I'm very cautious in asking you all these questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those people mostly went to take refuge somewhere where it was safe, because they were mostly civilians; women, children, and elderly persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're saying that they mostly went for safety reasons. So the people who would leave, did they leave because they had decided to go or was there a plan, an agreed plan for them to leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this was done under the Red Cross organisation, the convoy. So as the lists were drawn up stating -- now, who drew up the list stating who had the right to leave in a convoy, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You think that it was organised by the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mostly, they were the protagonists of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have just a little time before the break, but we can look at the next document, which to a large measure explains what Judge Antonetti was asking us about, and the document is 2D 1190.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Have you found the document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is, in fact, a very long list of persons travelling to Croatia, as it says, whereas it is a programme to deal with sick children, the elderly, and the infirm, and it is organised by the Red Cross of Bosnia-Herzegovina. So this is an enormous list, and it says "Split, Cairo, Croatia, Kiseljak." Anyway, we have the key. It says "Trnis, Split, Zagreb, France." It says where they're going. It's an enormous list of names; right, Mr. Pinjuh?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You recognise individuals on that list who left with the convoy, so let's look at page 26 now, please, and let me remind you that on page 26, there is the name of Mate Krasic. Do you know that he left?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, this document doesn't have a date. It's an enormous document. There are children, children who are chronically ill, children from various institutions, orphanages and so on, and a large number of vehicles with the license plates. Now, could you tell the Trial Chamber, under this name "Mr. Krasic," and perhaps anything else that you know, when this convoy was organised in Sarajevo and when it left? Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: I think this convoy was organised sometime in November 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Was there perhaps a family member of yours leaving in the convoy?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: I think that was the convoy that my father left in.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: He's not on the list? We tried to find him, but you can explain to us how that took place, the lists and so on.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: When it came to my father, as an elderly man he was no longer able to -- we were no longer able to help him in Sarajevo because we were taken up with our military duties, so I requested that he be included in the convoy so that he could leave Sarajevo by bus, and that was done.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Just one piece of -- more piece of information. On page 51 of this document, the document is signed by --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said that your father was an old man. How old was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was born in 1930.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So he was 62, 63. Well, that's young.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, he's my father, so --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But he wasn't a recruit or anything, so did you need permission and papers from the authorities, allowing you to leave?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. My father was retired in 1984 as an invalid.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Can you identify the author of this document on page 51? It says "Pero Butigan." Do you know the man, and do you know whether he was the president of the Red Cross at the end of 1992, as you say, when this convoy left?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: What page did you say?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Page 51.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it, and I know the man personally, I know Pero Butigan personally. He was the president of the Herzegovina Red Cross. Otherwise, he was a neighbour of mine in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And it says here that 2.075 individuals left on that particular occasion, and we have some additions with lists of children's names. So you know that, do you, that this was a very large convoy?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, it was certainly a large convoy, and I know that it reached its destination.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I might have 10 or 15 minutes more after the break, so I'd like to know whether we're going to take the break now, because I'm moving on to another area, my last area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We're going to have a 20-minute break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, were you a member of any associations or organisations linked to the rights of the defenders in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. I was a member of the Organisers of the Defence of the HVO in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I am the secretary of that organisation. Let me explain what kind of an association that is. The association is based -- or, rather, is bent on fighting for the rights of the fighters of the Croatian Defence Council, the defenders, and to protect the truth about the homeland war. That is the main -- and the dignity of the homeland war. That's the main premise, and that where any laws that are passed, are passed in agreement with and looking out for the defenders.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: As a member of this association, were you included in the drafting of any provisions regulating the rights of the defenders?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: We always advocate suitable provisions to regulate the rights of the defenders, so yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Are you a member of this association on behalf of the defenders of the HVO, the defenders of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Would you now take a look at document 2D1182, please. Have you found the document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It's a decree for pension requirements of members of the former Army of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and civil servants and employees of the former Federal Ministry of Defence, amendments to the decree on entitlement to an old-age pension under favourable conditions, et cetera. Would you explain to the Court what kind of decree this is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: This is a decree which the Government of the Federation proclaimed in order to enable former members of the Army of the Federation, higher-ranking commanders, generals, brigadiers, and defenders who had received decorations, that they can be entitled to an old age pension under favourable conditions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, does this decree regulate -- does it say what decorations are necessary, what commendation comes under the category which would enable persons to gain benefits?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, this decree did stipulate the decorations, medals, and so on would allow people to an entitlement to an old age pension under favourable conditions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Look at Article 1, please, now of this decree, and does it state specifically what those commendations include?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. Article 1 -- no, Article 1 does not specify, but they are listed under the law, the law governing decorations and commendations, and that law was passed in 2005.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, point 2 of Article 1, does it mention that particular law, the law you just mentioned, the Law on Special Rights of Recipients of War Commendations and Decorations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You also said that the decree regulates, and this what it says in point 3 of Article 1, which military positions entitle people to this kind of pension?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, that is enumerated here in Article 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now let's take a look at Article 7, and could you please tell us what the dead-line was for responding to this decree?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: They were duty-bound of complying by the 31st of March, 2007, and it stemmed from the day the law was published in the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now could we look at 2D1181, and could you explain to the Court what that was about? 2D01181 is the number of the next document.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: This is the same decree published again by the Government of the Federation in the Official Gazette due to certain changes, or, rather, amendments to this -- to the decree, but it specifies more or less the same rights.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Look at Article 4. Is the dead-line, the date, changed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. The dead-line for putting in a request has been extended to 2007, the 3rd of September.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, 2D1180 is the next document number I'd like us to look at. Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber what this document is, and what does it actually explain?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN PINJUH
utterances.text: This is a document issued by the Federation Government or, rather, the Ministry of the Defenders of the Government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and these are all the duties carried out by the defenders of the homeland war, and all of those who participated in the war would have special terms for retirement. And these are now those participants from the Croatian Defence Council.
